verses.english: “Mendicants, there are five kinds of hard-heartedness.

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati.
verses.english: Firstly, a mendicant has doubts about the Teacher. They’re uncertain, undecided, and lacking confidence.

verses.pali: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
verses.english: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

verses.pali: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ paṭhamo cetokhilo.
verses.english: This is the first kind of hard-heartedness.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhamme kaṅkhati …pe…
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant has doubts about the teaching …

verses.pali: sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto.
verses.english: A mendicant is angry and upset with their spiritual companions, resentful and closed off.

verses.pali: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
verses.english: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

verses.pali: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ pañcamo cetokhilo.
verses.english: This is the fifth kind of hard-heartedness.

verses.pali: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ cetokhilānaṁ pahānāya …pe… ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā”ti.
verses.english: To give up these five kinds of hard-heartedness you should develop the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …”
